name: Zheng Fan
current_role: Non-executive director, Li Auto Inc. (since Oct 2020)
profile: Fan Zheng is a co-founder of car portal Autohome, where he was vice president in charge of technology operations until 2016. He is a shareholder and non-executive (independent) director of EV maker Li Auto, founded by his longtime partner Li Xiang, which listed on Nasdaq in 2020 and in Hong Kong in 2021.
interesting_fact: His partnership with Li Auto CEO Li Xiang spans three companies: PCPOP.com, Autohome and now Li Auto, where he sits on the audit, compensation and nominating committees.
deep_cut_fact: Before Autohome he co-founded and was VP of PCPOP.com (2000-2005), the PC-hardware review site Li Xiang started as a teenager; Fan graduated from Hebei University of Science and Technology in 1999.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is via Li Auto IR. Sources differ on Autohome start date (1999 vs 2005).

name: Wong Kwong Yu
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, GOME Retail Holdings (HKEX: 0493)
profile: Wong Kwong Yu (Huang Guangyu) founded GOME, which grew from a single Beijing stall into China's largest consumer-electronics retail chain and made him China's richest man in the mid-2000s. He was convicted in 2010 and paroled in 2020; since his release he has sought to revive GOME's retail and e-commerce business.
interesting_fact: Time named him China's richest man in 2005; he had started GOME as a teenager with his brother after moving to Beijing from Shantou.
deep_cut_fact: GOME's first outlet opened on 1 January 1987 in a rented ~100 sq m shop on Zhushikou Street near Qianmen in Beijing; the 'GOME' (Guomei, 'beautiful country') brand name was only adopted in 1993.
notes: Highly sensitive history (2010 conviction, parole 2020); GOME is financially distressed. A general address info@gome.com.hk appears only on third-party quote pages (etnet), not verified on company site. Born Zeng Junlie, 1969, Shantou.

name: Qin Long
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and controlling shareholder (~43%), Qingdao Sentury Tire Co. (SZSE: 002984)
profile: Qin Long founded Qingdao Sentury Tire in 2007, building it from a manual tire plant in Qingdao into a listed maker of passenger, motorsport and aircraft tires with factories in Qingdao, Thailand and elsewhere. Sentury listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020; he directly and indirectly controls about 43% of the company.
interesting_fact: Sentury is one of the few Chinese firms making aircraft tires, alongside motorsport tires, and it pursued an overseas-factory strategy with a heavily automated plant in Rayong, Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Qin was reportedly the only one in his management team backing a fully automated 'Dream Factory'; after automating Qingdao's green-tire handling (utilisation rose from 72% to 96.5%) he copied it to Thailand. Quote: 'I have orders and I will lose the customers if I cannot deliver the tires.'
notes: IR email belongs to the board secretary's office (board secretary Wang Qian). Chairman title last explicitly confirmed in 2025 filings; 2026 interim report lists him as legal representative and controller. Cimcorp source is a vendor case study.

name: Wang Qian
current_role: Founder and CEO, X Square Robot (Zibianliang Jiqiren), Shenzhen
profile: Wang Qian, a Tsinghua and USC-trained robotics researcher, ran a quant fund in the US before closing it in 2023 to found X Square Robot in Shenzhen. The embodied-AI startup builds general-purpose robot foundation models (WALL-A, open-sourced WALL-OSS) and reached a valuation above US$2.8bn in 2026, with backers including Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan and Xiaomi.
interesting_fact: He argues humanoid robots doing repetitive factory work are 'just a PR stunt' and that the field should focus on generalisation; X Square raised four consecutive rounds to pass a $2.8bn valuation by mid-2026.
deep_cut_fact: As a researcher he was among the early adopters of attention mechanisms in neural networks, publishing at the same 2014 conference as Google's early attention paper; after leaving robotics for finance he said 'I couldn't sleep for nights. I regretted not pursuing robotics full time.'
notes: Highly relevant to an AI/compute-themed podcast (embodied AI foundation models). No published personal net worth found; the list source is not Forbes. Pandaily attention-mechanism claim is from a paywalled profile (visible portion).

name: Wang Weiyao
current_role: Founder and chairman, Jiangsu World Group (Wode / 沃得集团), Danyang, Jiangsu
profile: Wang Weiyao (王伟耀, b. 1963, Danyang) founded World Group, a Danyang-based machinery conglomerate whose World Agricultural Machinery unit is one of China's largest makers of rice combine harvesters; it also makes forging presses (World Precision Machinery), construction and garden machinery, auto parts and develops property.
interesting_fact: He built World Group from a small textile-machinery accessories workshop founded in 1988 into a group with ~20,000 staff; its harvesters are sold across China and exported to dozens of countries.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing Picheng Middle School in 1982, his first venture was the Danyang Textile Machinery Accessories Factory (1988); he later added crankshaft, filter and kitchen-equipment plants before moving into combine harvesters in 1997. He holds an MBA from Nanjing University of Science and Technology and a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: Identity inferred from 'World' source-of-wealth label (no Forbes bio in input); Wang Weiyao of World (Wode) Group is the only strong match. Very private; Chinese-language outreach via group website contact page likely best.

name: Li Shijiang
current_role: Director and actual controller of Do-Fluoride New Materials (SZSE: 002407); chairman of parent Jiaozuo Do-Fluoride Industrial Group
profile: Li Shijiang (b. 1950, Wen County, Henan) turned the state-owned Jiaozuo Cryolite Factory into Do-Fluoride (DFD), a leading maker of fluorine chemicals and of lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6), the key salt in lithium-ion battery electrolyte. He chaired the listed company from 2007 until handing over the chair in Dec 2025; he remains a director and controls the parent group.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he went to Japan to buy LiPF6 production technology, was turned away, then assembled his own team, which spent about eight years cracking the process, making DFD one of the world's largest LiPF6 suppliers for EV batteries.
deep_cut_fact: Before chemicals he served five years in the PLA Second Artillery (1968-73), then rose through the Wen County fertilizer plant (equipment and technical sections, petrochemical plant director) and a paper mill; he also chairs the council of Henan Polytechnic University's New Materials Industry College.
notes: Age 76. Strong battery-supply-chain angle. Military-service detail is from Chinese media profiles; the annual report confirms the career path. Listed company chairmanship changed hands in Dec 2025.
